rationale: The source gives a partial order as a reflexive, antisymmetric, transitive binary relation, the induced strict order, comparability, and total order exactly as in the Definition. Definition only.

The source defines a chain/totally ordered subset by pairwise comparability, exactly the item's Definition. The empty-set convention is the vacuous instance of that quantified definition. Definition only.

The source gives upper bound and least upper bound/supremum with the same ambient-poset membership, universal quantifiers, and leastness direction. The item uses those definitions and, after A8 repair, explicitly derives the equivalence between being an upper bound outside the set and being a strict upper bound. Definition only.

The sources distinguish maximal (nothing strictly above) from greatest (above every element), give the equivalent maximality implication, and define the dual notions exactly as the item does. Definition only.

The sources define chain completeness as existence of a supremum for every chain and call x <= f(x) inflationary/progressive. Convention delta: many sources require a nonempty poset and/or only nonempty chains; the item includes the empty chain, derives bottom = sup(empty), and merges the progressive-map definition into the same item. These are semantically equivalent under the stated convention, but more than cosmetic editing.

Khatchatourian Definition 2.1 and the Wikipedia definition give a function on a family of nonempty sets selecting an element of each member, exactly the Definition; the on-X formulation is the specialization to all nonempty subsets. Alpha materially narrowed the first Remark after A7 so it now attributes only natural-number-indexed finite choice to lem-finite-choice, matching that local lemma rather than importing the general finite-family identification. The component is therefore ai-altered with semantic-source evidence.

Khatchatourian's (AC) and the Wikipedia statement say exactly that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the nonempty-product formulation is the standard equivalent recorded by both treatments. This is an axiom/definition item and has no proof component.

The source states that every finite collection of nonempty sets has a choice function in ZF and is proved by induction. Convention delta: the item avoids an unavailable abstract finiteness definition and states the exact listable form using a function with von Neumann ordinal domain n, allowing repeated values. Its proof is the sourced induction materially expanded with restriction and an overwrite construction that handles repetitions.

The Mathlib Bourbaki-Witt development and Zubir's published guide define admissible subsets by closure under the progressive map and suprema of chains, with a chosen base point. Convention delta: the item works in the empty-chain convention, so membership of bottom is forced by supremum closure and replaces the separate base-point condition. This is a semantic specialization, not merely notation. Definition only.

Mathlib defines the bottom admissible set as the intersection of all admissible sets and proves it admissible; Zubir likewise constructs M as that intersection and proves it is the smallest admissible subset. Delta: the sources carry an explicit base point/nonempty-chain convention, while the item specializes the base to bottom through the empty-chain convention. The local proof is the same intersection argument, phase-stratified and adapted to that convention.

Mathlib's IsExtremePt gives exactly membership in the bottom admissible set and f(z) <= y for every earlier z; its bot_eq_of_le_or_map_le theorem uses exactly the cut z <= y or f(y) <= z. Zubir Definition/Stage 1 uses the same extremal point and M_c. Delta: the item has specialized the literature's base-point presentation to M generated from bottom, so the combined Definition is semantically identical but materially adapted.

Zubir's Lemma 1 proves the cut M_c admissible and its first closure calculation is precisely f(M_c) subset M_c; Mathlib packages the resulting cut equality as IsExtremePt.bot_eq_of_le_or_map_le. Delta: the item extracts the map-closure subclaim into a standalone lemma and uses the bottom/empty-chain convention. The proof follows the sourced below/equal/above case split with explicit order axioms.

Zubir's Lemma 1 proves M_c admissible and its supremum-closure half is exactly the two cases used here: all chain elements are below c, or one lies on the f(c)-upper side. Delta: the item extracts that half as a standalone lemma and includes the empty chain through its convention. The local phase proof is a materially reformatted sourced argument.

Mathlib IsExtremePt.bot_eq_of_le_or_map_le states that the set of z in the bottom admissible set satisfying z <= y or f(y) <= z equals that bottom set; Zubir Lemma 1 states M_c=M. This is exactly the conclusion after specializing the literature's base-point convention to bottom. The proof follows the sourced admissibility-plus-minimality argument, phase-stratified locally.

Zubir Lemma 2(b) proves that if c is extreme then f(c) is extreme, using M=M_c to rule out a point between c and f(c), followed by the strict/equality split; Mathlib folds the same subclaim into admissibility of the set of extreme points. The item extracts and fully stratifies that sourced subargument.

Zubir Lemma 2(c) proves that the supremum of a chain of extreme points is extreme; Mathlib packages the same closure under admissibility of all extreme points. Delta: the item isolates this closure component, includes the empty chain, and uses the equivalent witness x not <= y route rather than Zubir's displayed quantifier-negation route. The proof is materially adapted from the sourced argument.

Mathlib setOf_isExtremePt_eq_bot and Zubir Lemma 2 state that the extreme points are exactly the smallest/bottom admissible set. Delta: the item phrases only the every-element direction as its title/Statement and supplies the reverse inclusion by definition inside the proof; its empty-chain convention removes the separate base case. The proof is the sourced closure-and-minimality proof, phase-stratified.

Zubir Theorem 2 and the Lang/Mathlib Bourbaki-Witt development prove that the smallest admissible set is totally ordered after all its points are shown extreme. Delta: the item's chain convention includes empty and it makes the progressivity bridge x <= f(x) explicit. The proof is a phase-stratified adaptation of the sourced two-line argument.

Wikipedia states exactly that a chain-complete nonempty poset and an inflationary/progressive self-map have a fixed point, without monotonicity; the item's empty-chain convention already implies nonemptiness. Zubir/Lang supply the smallest-admissible-set proof used locally. The proof is materially decomposed into local lemmas and phase-stratified, so it is ai-altered rather than a cosmetic transcription.

Encyclopedia of Mathematics states the same nonempty-poset hypothesis, upper bound for every totally ordered subset, and maximal-element conclusion, and records equivalence with AC. Wikipedia's Bourbaki-Witt article gives the same fixed-point route through the inclusion poset of chains. The local proof materially combines the two stages and explicitly handles equal strict-upper-bound sets, so the proof is ai-altered.

Khatchatourian pp.10-11 and the Stanford Encyclopedia give exactly this direction: order partial choice functions by extension, union every chain, take a maximal element by Zorn, and extend it unless its domain is the whole family. The item expands that standard sourced proof into a phase-stratified contradiction and verifies the order axioms explicitly.

Both sources state that the Axiom of Choice and Zorn's lemma are equivalent over ZF, exactly the corollary. The three-step local proof simply composes the two already established dependency directions and was formulated locally rather than following a distinct sourced proof.

Encyclopedia of Mathematics records Zorn's lemma as equivalent to AC, while Cohen's 1963 paper is the primary forcing source for relative consistency of not-AC. Together they semantically establish, under Con(ZF), the negation of the displayed false claim. Delta: the item packages those two established results as a pedagogical false-statement/refutation and makes the consistency qualification explicit. The short contradiction chaining the local equivalence with Cohen is locally written.

The sources explicitly state that maximal must not be confused with greatest, that multiple maximal elements can occur, and that the notions coincide in a total order, exactly negating the bannered claim. The source's discrete-poset examples specialize to the item's two-element antichain; the local verification expands that standard witness, so its proof is ai-altered.

The specific three-set family and displayed graph g are a bespoke checkable example rather than a sourced construction. Its current consumer cone has size 1, consisting of the direct citation from lem-finite-choice; that citation is explanatory rather than a logical proof dependency. It fits generation.role=example.

Khatchatourian Example 2.2(3) states exactly that for A=P(N) without empty, f(A)=min(A) is a choice function; the following discussion explains that a definable least-element rule needs no AC. The item materially expands this one-line sourced proof into existence, uniqueness, Separation, and graph checks, hence proof ai-altered.

Khatchatourian gives the left-shoe rule, the socks contrast, and the role of a definable rule; the Stanford Encyclopedia gives Russell's shoes/socks account; Jech is the cited source for the countable-pairs permutation/symmetric-model independence fact. Delta: the item merges the illustration with a formal Separation proof for distinguished members and a carefully qualified external ZF-independence clause. Its verification is an expanded adaptation of those sourced arguments.

The complete-lattice source states that the power set ordered by inclusion has arbitrary joins given by union (and meets by intersection), exactly implying the item's stronger claim and its chain-complete specialization, including bottom empty. The local proof expands the standard union upper-bound and leastness checks, so it is ai-altered.

Zubir's Zorn proof constructs the chains of a poset ordered by inclusion and proves that the union of an inclusion-chain is again a chain and is its least upper bound; Wikipedia describes the same intermediate poset. Convention delta: Zubir collects nonempty chains, while the item includes the empty chain and obtains bottom=empty. The proof is a fully expanded phase-stratified version of the sourced union argument.

The sources give discrete singleton-subset posets with multiple incomparable maximal elements and no greatest element, and the general rule that several maximal elements preclude a greatest one. Delta: the item specializes the standard proper-subsets construction to P({1,2}) with the top deleted, retaining empty as a bottom. Its direct inclusion verification is the corresponding sourced example worked out in detail.

Delta: the item combines these standard facts to isolate N itself as the unbounded offending chain and proves the claim from its locally constructed arithmetic order. The proof is a material phase-stratified expansion.
